title: All rooms should span every hostel, with a hostel filter, and move to the Property tab
description: Product Owner request, three changes to All rooms: show rooms across all hostels rather than only the selected one; add a filter to narrow to a hostel; and move the entry point to the Property tab. CURRENT STATE: AllRoomsViewModel takes a hostelId from the nav route and queries getByHostelIdWithFloor(hostelId), so the screen is hostel-scoped by construction. Reaching it means Property > pick a hostel > All rooms, which is exactly the drill-down LODGY-40 set out to remove - it just removed one level of it rather than two. Widening the query and adding a filter finishes that job. IMPLEMENTATION NOTES: the repository needs an all-hostels equivalent of getByHostelIdWithFloor, and the room rows need to carry their hostel so tiles can be grouped or labelled - a room number alone is ambiguous once two properties are on screen, since both can have a 101. The occupancy flow observeRoomOccupancyByHostel is likewise per-hostel and needs the same widening. The RAG tiles and summary from LODGY-67 carry over unchanged; the summary should follow the filter rather than always reporting the whole estate. OPEN QUESTION for the PO: with the screen no longer hostel-scoped, whether the hostel-level 'All rooms' action disappears entirely or stays as a shortcut that opens the screen pre-filtered to that hostel. The second keeps the useful path from a hostel you are already inside.
acceptanceCriteria: All rooms lists rooms from every hostel by default, not only the selected one
A hostel filter narrows the view, including an all-hostels option, and the empty/part-full/full summary reflects the current filter rather than the whole estate
Each tile identifies which hostel its room belongs to, so two properties with a room 101 are not confusable
The screen is reachable directly from the Property tab without first opening a hostel
Tapping a tile still opens that room's bed grid regardless of which hostel it is in
Correct in dark mode and in Hindi, and the tiles stay legible once a hostel name is added to them
A warden with a single hostel sees no regression - the filter is unobtrusive and the screen still reads as it does today

history.note: Filed at the Product Owner's request: All rooms should span every hostel with a hostel filter, and move to the Property tab. Notes which repository and occupancy queries are hostel-scoped today and need widening.

Cross-reference: LODGY-72 adds a vacancy filter to this same screen, driven from the Home tile. Design the hostel filter and the fill filter together - two separately-conceived filter rows on one screen will not sit well, and both need to feed the LODGY-67 summary row consistently.

DECIDED: the per-hostel 'All rooms' action stays, opening the screen pre-filtered to that hostel. It is the useful path when the warden is already inside a property, and it costs nothing once the filter exists.
Starting. Built together since both change All rooms: hostel filter + vacancy filter, moved to Property, Home tile routes here, VacantViewScreen removed and LODGY-59 notification repointed.

Built together with the other, since both change All rooms and splitting them would have meant two filter rows designed apart. AllRoomsViewModel is no longer hostel-scoped by construction: new RoomDao.getAllWithFloor() and BedDao.observeRoomOccupancy() cover every property, RoomWithFloor now carries hostelId/hostelName, and both filters live in UI state so they compose. The nav route became optional-arg: no hostelId means every hostel, hasSpace=true pre-filters. LODGY-70 specifics: reachable from the Property tab top bar without opening a hostel first; the per-hostel shortcut survives pre-filtered, as decided; tiles prefix the hostel ONLY when the view spans several, so a filtered view is not cluttered with a name it already states in the header. LODGY-72 specifics: the Home vacant-beds tile now opens here with has-space applied. 'Has space' is EMPTY plus PARTIAL, not EMPTY alone - a partly filled room still has a bed free. On the beds-vs-rooms mismatch the ticket warned about, the summary counts ROOMS and the state also exposes vacantBedsInView so the two can be reconciled rather than silently disagreeing. VacantViewScreen, its ViewModel and its test are deleted. Its ROUTE_VACANT_VIEW is kept as a REDIRECT to All rooms rather than removed - LODGY-59's vacancy notification puts that route in its intent, and a notification already sitting on a warden's phone would otherwise open nothing after they update. Verified that redirect works. VERIFIED ON DEVICE, all four paths: Home tile arrives with the has-space chip selected and Moonlight's full room excluded (18 of 19 rooms); Property tab opens unfiltered showing all 19 including the full one; hostel filter narrows and composes with the space filter (Moonlight + has-space correctly shows nothing, since its only room is full); and the old notification route lands on All rooms. Tiles read 'Sunrise PG · Ground' when spanning, plain 'Ground' when filtered. Correct in Hindi throughout. TESTS: 5 new covering all-hostels default, hostel narrowing, has-space including partials, the hasSpace arrival argument, and the room-vs-bed count distinction. Full suite 438 pass, coverage 96.89% line. NOT SCHEMA-AFFECTING: the new DAO methods are reads over existing tables, no entity changed, database stays at version 4, no migration.

PASS - verified on the emulator against a two-hostel estate (Sunrise PG 18 rooms, Moonlight 1), in Hindi and in dark mode. AC1: All rooms opens listing both hostels' rooms with no hostel chosen. AC2: the hostel chips narrow it AND the summary tracks the filter - all = 16 empty/1 partial/2 full, Moonlight = 0/0/1, Sunrise = 16/1/1. AC3: every tile carries its hostel ('Sunrise PG - First'), and when one hostel is selected the tiles drop the now-redundant prefix and show only the floor - a nice touch beyond the AC. AC4: reached from the Property tab top bar without opening a hostel first. AC5: tapping tile 102 opened that room's bed grid (DOUBLE, Rs 5500/bed, Bed A vacant, Bed B occupied), matching the tile's '2 me 1 khali' label. AC6: dark mode and Hindi both correct - the RAG tiles stay legible with the hostel name added, and each tile pairs its colour with a status icon rather than relying on colour alone. AC7: AllRoomsScreen.kt:84 hides the hostel filter row entirely when hostels.size <= 1, so a single-hostel warden sees no new control at all.
